html:
The Land War was a campaign by Irish tenant farmers from 1879 to 1882 for fair rents and secure tenure, led by the Irish National Land League.

Bad harvests and falling prices threatened a new famine in the west. Michael Davitt began the movement in County Mayo in 1879, and Charles Stewart Parnell became its president. Tenants refused unfair rents and shunned anyone who took over the farm of an evicted family. The first victim was a land agent called Captain Boycott, which gave English a new word.

The British government passed land acts that cut rents. Later acts lent tenants money to buy their farms, and by the early 1900s most Irish farmers owned their land. The landlord class created by the Cromwellian settlement faded away. The movement fed the drive for Home Rule. See Ireland.
sum: The Land War was a campaign by Irish tenant farmers from 1879 to 1882 for fair rents and secure tenure, led by the Irish National Land League.
